SAB_composition_precedence: For a combined pair, duplicate the original first denomination (M04), remove all occurrences of the original maximum (M03), remove denominations equal to amount (M05), apply the unsorted prefix break (M06), apply the M07 guard using the original minimum, then combine recurrence modifiers M01/M02/M08. This is an explicit proposal-level semantic merge rule; exact source-diff compatibility still requires review against each parent implementation.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Change the coefficient/base state for amount 0 from 1 to 0.

family_adapters.K1: dp[0]=0; also change explicit amount==0 or empty-prefix returns from 1 to 0 (notably G04 and G07)

mutation_taxonomy.name: Empty-combination identity set to zero
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1 amount-zero/boundary and every reachable positive stratum D2, D4, D5, D6, D7 and D8. The wrong identity suppresses positive counts; D3 is unchanged because its reference count is zero.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: A direct base-state fault; should be localized in each family.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: The correct reference answer is positive; the incorrect zero identity then removes every derivation from the empty state.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Replace unlimited reuse of each denomination by at-most-one use per denomination.

family_adapters.K1: in-place parents: descending amount update; double-buffer G06: use previous-row value prev[a-c] rather than same-pass cur[a-c]
family_adapters.K2: use branch reads previous row T[i-1][a-c_i]
family_adapters.K4: replace each geometric factor by (1+x^c); doubling variants retain only the one-use factor
family_adapters.K5: use finite-use factor updates in each half-product

mutation_taxonomy.name: Unbounded multiplicity reduced to one use
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1/D2 boundary and exact-match cases, D4 modular cases, D5 non-greedy cases, and D6-D8 where a valid representation requires repeated use. D3 remains unchanged because restricting a solution set cannot make an unreachable target reachable.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: Same intended semantic error, translated to each recurrence.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: At least one valid combination requires using some denomination at least twice, and the at-most-once count is lower than the unbounded count.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Remove the maximum denomination before evaluating the otherwise unchanged parent.

family_adapters.K1: skip max denomination in outer coin loop
family_adapters.K3: omit max denomination from recursion state
family_adapters.K5: omit it from the appropriate half-product

mutation_taxonomy.name: Largest denomination omitted
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1, D2, D4-D8 when the largest denomination contributes to at least one valid representation. It cannot create a solution on D3 unreachable inputs.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: Order-independent because max(coins) is determined by value, not input position.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: At least one valid combination uses the maximum denomination, so removing it changes the answer.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Process the first input denomination twice as if the two occurrences were distinct coin types, despite the contract's distinct-denomination set semantics.

family_adapters.K1: repeat first coin's in-place update pass
family_adapters.K3: include first denomination twice as two recursion indices
family_adapters.K4: multiply by the first geometric factor twice
family_adapters.K5: include first denomination factor twice in its half-product

mutation_taxonomy.name: First denomination processed twice
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1, D2, D4-D8 whenever the first denomination participates in a representation; duplicating its type changes the count. It cannot make D3 reachable because denomination values are unchanged.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: A localized repeated-iteration defect; preserve original input order when identifying the first denomination.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: The first input denomination participates in at least one representation, and treating it as two distinct types changes the combination count.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Discard any denomination c equal to the target amount A before counting combinations, incorrectly treating an exact denomination match as unusable.

family_adapters.K1: filter target-equal denomination before the coin loop
family_adapters.K3: omit target-equal coin index from recursion state
family_adapters.K4: omit target-equal factor from the generating-function product
family_adapters.K5: omit target-equal factor before splitting and half-products

mutation_taxonomy.name: Target-equal denomination omitted
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1/D2 exact-match boundaries and D4/D6-D8 inputs where a denomination equals the target. The fixed D5 {1,3,4}, amount 6/10 examples contain no target-equal denomination; D3 remains unchanged because its answer is zero.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: Distinct from M03: it removes only c=A, even when a larger denomination remains; the two coincide only when the target-equal denomination is also the maximum.
mutation_taxonomy.semantic_edit: coins := [c for c in coins if c != amount]
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: A positive target denomination is present; removing it removes the singleton combination using that denomination.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Before the parent performs any ordering/normalization, scan the original input sequence and stop at the first denomination greater than amount; retain only the prefix. No sort is performed before this test.
mutation_taxonomy.name: Unsorted prefix early-stop
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1, D2, D4, D6, D7 and D8 when an input ordering places a denomination greater than amount before a later useful denomination. The fixed D5 {1,3,4}, amount 6/10 examples contain no coin greater than amount; D3 remains zero either way.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: Must execute before all sorting/bisect/filtering in S0; otherwise it may be repaired by the parent normalization.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: A denomination greater than the target appears before a later denomination that contributes to a valid representation; the premature break then discards that useful suffix.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Incorrectly return zero whenever amount is not divisible by min(coins), treating divisibility by the smallest denomination as necessary for reachability.
mutation_taxonomy.name: Minimum-denomination divisibility shortcut
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1, D2, D4, D6, D7 and D8 when a reachable amount is not divisible by the smallest denomination. The fixed D5 examples contain denomination 1; D3 is correctly zero under this guard.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: This is deliberately a false-negative pruning rule; it does not alter inputs or the oracle.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: The target is not divisible by the minimum denomination, but the reference answer is positive because other denominations form a valid combination.

mutation_taxonomy.definition: Multiply every non-empty use-transition contribution by two instead of one, overcounting denomination-use paths.

family_adapters.K4: residue-chain: new[a]=old[a]+2*new[a-c]; binary-doubling: replace each factor (1-x^c)^-1 by product_j(1+2^(2^j)*x^(2^j*c)); sparse carrier: coefficient at multiplicity t is weighted by 2^t
family_adapters.K5: apply the same doubled geometric-factor coefficients in each half-product before the Cauchy product

mutation_taxonomy.name: Use-transition contribution doubled
mutation_taxonomy.reach: D1, D2, D4-D8 whenever the correct answer includes at least one denomination-use transition; D3 remains zero and is unchanged.
mutation_taxonomy.risk: A transition-weight fault distinct from duplicating one denomination: each positive multiplicity path is reweighted.
mutation_taxonomy.trigger_condition: The reference answer is positive; every non-empty transition path receives an extra multiplicity weight, changing the total.

orientation_rule: Balanced base tournament orientation; the second occurrence of each repeated pair is reversed. The mechanism placed in SA is M01..M08 as recorded per row, not always the lower-numbered mechanism.
